groups.sentence: Instructors decide whether and how generative AI is used in their courses, from prohibiting to encouraging it.
Instructors decide, define and develop a clear AI policy for their course and are responsible for communicating it.
Instructors may set different AI rules for different assignments within the same course.
Instructors consider and provide assignment-level AI guidance rather than only a course-wide rule.
Instructors may adopt or adapt the provided sample AI syllabus statements to fit their course.
Instructors may prohibit AI use entirely or strictly restrict it in their courses.
Universities preserve faculty autonomy and avoid imposing one-size-fits-all AI rules.
Instructors state clearly to students whether and how AI may be used, including for each assignment.
Students use generative AI only on assignments or in ways the instructor permits.
Students follow the AI usage rules set for each assignment by the instructor or syllabus.
Teaching assistants and consultants follow the instructor's AI decisions and expectations.
Decisions about AI misuse and its consequences are left to the instructor's course policy.
AI rules differ across courses, instructors, disciplines and assignments, with no single approach.
The university sets no single AI policy and leaves decisions on AI use to faculty.
